title: Booking a Home Energy Visit
transcript:
Good afternoon. I received a leaflet about your home energy advice visits. Our flat feels cold even when the heating has been on for several hours. I would like to know whether your service could help us.
We can look at how heat is being used and suggest practical changes. The visit is for advice, so the adviser will not carry out building work or try to sell you a new heating system.
That's exactly what I need. I rent the flat, and I don't think I can make major changes without asking the owner. Can tenants book the visit, or does the landlord have to contact you first?
Tenants can book directly. Please have a recent bill ready, because it helps the adviser understand how much energy the household uses. You can cover your account number if you would prefer to keep that private.
I can find one. Will you need access to every room? My partner sometimes works from home, and I would like to choose a time when the visit won't interrupt an important online meeting.
The adviser needs to see the main living areas and inspect the windows. There is no need to move furniture away from every wall. If one room is occupied, we can return to it near the end.
That should be manageable. Are appointments available at weekends? During the week I leave home quite early and usually don't return until after six, when most offices have already closed.
We offer one Saturday each month, and there are two appointments left this month. The visit normally takes about an hour. Afterwards, we send a report by email, so you don't have to remember every suggestion.
I would like the later appointment. Does the report include estimates of what each change might cost? It would be easier to speak to the landlord if I could show which improvements are relatively simple.
Yes, we separate changes you can make yourself from work requiring permission. Costs are only approximate, since prices vary. We also explain which measures are likely to make the greatest difference in your particular flat.
The leaflet says the service is free, but is that only for people receiving financial support? We both work, so I wasn't sure whether we would qualify for the same scheme.
The first advice visit is free for all district residents. Financial assistance for installing improvements has separate conditions. The adviser can explain those, but booking this visit does not automatically qualify you for a grant.
